platform: instagram (rules also used for Facebook copies)

assumptions.claim: Feed captions are cut behind 'more' after roughly 125 characters, so the first line must work on its own under 125.
Reels show even less caption over the video; keep the first line under 55 characters.
assumptions.source: Mark's brief; reels overlay shows about one short line (https://www.clipspeed.ai/blog/instagram-reels-captions.html)

assumptions.claim: Instagram captions allow up to 2,200 characters.
No hashtags. Instagram capped posts and reels at 5 hashtags (Dec 2025) and its head says hashtags do not increase reach; plain search words in the caption do the work. Same on Facebook.

assumptions.value: plain search phrases such as 'what to sow in November UK', 'growing garlic in pots'
assumptions.claim: Captions carry the words people type into Instagram search.
assumptions.source: Mark's brief; Instagram search reads captions (https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/instagram-implements-new-limits-on-hashtag-use/808309/)

assumptions.claim: One ask per caption, rotating save / send / comment. Sends per reach is one of the most important ranking signals.
Name the site as plain text (homegrownplate.co.uk) instead of 'link in bio'.
Vertical 9:16 reels, best shot first, hook as large text in the first 2 seconds because many watch muted.
4:5 portrait slides take the most feed space.
Reels Tue and Fri, carousels Wed and Sun, Stories daily 09:00.
